description:
## Reproducer and affected execution path
Discovered while implementing zaq-o9d.4, a test-only Telegram driver in epic zaq-o9d.
File: test/zaq/channels/integration/providers/telegram_test.exs, test "mention-required policy admits an actual native group mention".
Native webhook: supergroup chat -100123, sender 456, text "@zaq Mention question", entities [%{"type" => "mention", "offset" => 0, "length" => 4}]. Saved connector settings set bot_name "zaq", bot_user_id "999", room_reply_policy "mention_required". The real Jido.Chat.Telegram.Adapter, JidoChatBridge/State, CommunicationBridge, NodeRouter, Engine and local LLM endpoint are used; no internal modules are mocked.

## Expected and observed
Expected: a valid native bot mention is admitted for the configured conversation-enabled agent and produces the normal provider reply/confirmed shared transcript.
Observed: webhook is acknowledged, the message is captured as passive history, and no ExecutionRecord/LLM request/final reply is created.
The same driver successfully exercises direct messages and group mentions with default reply policy. No runtime sleeps or synthetic normalized mention flag is used.

## Source-backed diagnosis
deps/jido_chat_telegram/lib/jido/chat/telegram/adapter.ex transform_message/1 constructs Jido.Chat.Incoming without deriving was_mentioned/mentions from the native message; Incoming defaults was_mentioned to false.
deps/jido_chat/lib/jido/chat/handler_dispatch.ex mentioned?/2 recognizes "@zaq" text and invokes the mention handler.
lib/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge.ex handle_mention_event/3 forwards the unchanged Incoming. handle_message_event/4's mention_required gate then rejects it because incoming.was_mentioned remains false.
Normalization/admission ownership needs a deliberate fix; do not modify a fake to synthesize the missing production evidence.

## Validation evidence
mix test test/zaq/channels/integration test/zaq/channels/telegram_history_delivery_test.exs test/zaq/channels/telegram_markdown_delivery_test.exs: 38 tests + 1 property, 1 failure, solely this new policy reproducer. Existing Telegram tests and new default direct/shared paths pass. The reproducer now fails on missing prepared execution immediately after synchronous ingress rather than waiting for an LLM timeout.

## Authorization and scope
This is a recorded blocker, not authorization to change production. The user explicitly restricted epic zaq-o9d to test/** plus the named Mix-task/skill tooling exceptions. Application modules, dependency source/pins/config are outside that scope.
A production fix needs explicit user authorization as separate scoped work. Keep the reproducer and do not skip it, weaken it, unregister Telegram, inject was_mentioned into the fake native payload, or patch production under the test-infrastructure ticket. Preserve identity/permission defaults.
Read AGENTS.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/services/channels.md and docs/agent-tools.md before diagnosis/fix. Cross-provider regression validation is required after an authorized correction.

comments.text: Final validation snapshot: canonical mix q passes. Combined current integration + existing Mattermost and Telegram delivery/history regressions run 75 tests + 2 properties, with exactly the two new Telegram reproducer failures (zaq-kxd and zaq-imv). Existing tests pass. This bug blocks zaq-o9d.4. No application or dependency files were changed; a fix requires separate explicit user authorization.

title: [zaq-kxd] Telegram mention_required drops native group bot mentions before agent admission
